theCorrectionsThisCheckpointForced.what: The pin recorded four factory facts that nothing checked.
theCorrectionsThisCheckpointForced.howFound: Reading the drift check against its own header: `facts.refusalCode` and `facts.unmeasuredCode` were recorded in PROGRAM_DECLARATION_PIN but no leg compared anything to them, which is the P-320 arrangement ('a second copy is a number that can drift') one layer down.
theCorrectionsThisCheckpointForced.fix: Added REFUSAL_CODES to the declaration and `scanForRefusalCodeDrift` as a drift-check leg, plus a test for each direction. The leg checks that every `refuse(...)` in the guard passes a declared code identifier and that every declared code is thrown somewhere.
theCorrectionsThisCheckpointForced.findingThatCameOutOfIt: The guard's own helper `function refuse(code, message, detail)` matched the throw-site regex as a call, so the first version of the leg refused the committed tree with 'the guard throws undeclared refusal code(s) code'. That is the check working on its first run, and it is recorded because the fix (strip the helper declaration before reading call sites) is the kind of thing that must not be a silent narrowing. The leg now also matches a hand-spelled STRING code at a throw site, which the identifier-only version would have missed.

theCorrectionsThisCheckpointForced.what: The engine's refusal code NAMES differ from the factory's and that was about to be silently smoothed over.
theCorrectionsThisCheckpointForced.detail: The factory refuses DESTRUCTIVE_BLAST_RADIUS / DESTRUCTIVE_UNMEASURED (recorded in the pin); the engine throws BLAST_RADIUS_EXCEEDED / BLAST_RADIUS_UNMEASURED (P-213, named in live messages and asserted by P-213's and P-275's tests). The dispatch requires the NUMBER and the TOKEN FORMAT to be the program's; it does not require four code names to change. Renaming them to match a string would touch every caller and test for no measured effect on any refusal. STATED in the declaration with the reason, and the single-source half was taken instead: the guard no longer writes a code literal at a throw site.

theCorrectionsThisCheckpointForced.what: CP1's enumeration plan said 'enumerate ... or wired'. The first scan that implemented it flagged TEN modules, and only two of them were in class.
theCorrectionsThisCheckpointForced.detail: The scan's `UPDATE atoms` pattern matched five in-place field rewrites (SET body = ...) on rows that stay served: backfill-bastrop-zoning-fact-code-refs/-provenance, backfill-property-line-tags-bastrop, restamp-bastrop-downtown-zoning, strip-cad-parcel-roll-owner-fields, backfill-icc-access-policy. They are destructive EDITS, not destructive STATUS changes, and P-328's enumeration asks for writers that set a destructive status on a served record. The pattern was narrowed to a destructive status literal, `DELETE FROM atoms`, or an UPDATE that sets a destructive status -- and the five are named in the declaration as a RECORDED EXCLUSION rather than merely not matched, so a reader can disagree with the judgement instead of it being invisible.
theCorrectionsThisCheckpointForced.andTheOtherTwo: Two flagged modules WERE in class and are now registered: write-building-footprint-county.mjs (a set-valued, county-scoped DELETE of absence atoms superseded by present atoms minted in the same run) and migrate-bastrop-road-legacy-synthetic-ids.mjs (a single named predecessor row, deleted only after its replacement is verified readable). Both keep `wired: false` with a reason in the register.

theProducersBypassAndWhatWasDoneAboutIt.cp1Wording: 'The refusal is a CALL-SITE convention, not a property of the producer: reconcileCountyParcelNodes is pure and returns orphans with no measurement attached, so any new caller that imports it and retires what it returns re-opens the hole silently.'
theProducersBypassAndWhatWasDoneAboutIt.whatWasDone: NAMED AND PINNED, not closed, and the reasoning is that closing it in the type system is a different change than this row: the guard's return shape would have to carry an unforgeable authorisation, and the two CLI writers are the only callers today. What the row does instead is make the register's scope explicit (the producers are named as `producer` on each entry) plus a test that refuses an UNREGISTERED module carrying a destructive statement -- so a new writer file that retires anything is caught by the suite even if its author never reads this declaration. A future writer that imports the producer and writes without the guard is caught by that scan, because the retire WRITE is the statement the scan looks for.
theProducersBypassAndWhatWasDoneAboutIt.stillOpen: A module that retires rows through an imported helper whose own file has the statement (as write-road-node-county.mjs does with storage's retireRoadNodeInstance) is caught by the helper's entry, not by the caller's. That is stated in the register entry, and it is why the register names both the CLI and the body builder rather than choosing one.

A refusal writes nothing.
whatBypassesIt: A caller of reconcileCountyParcelNodes / reconcileCountyRoadNodes that retires what it returns without calling the guard -- named, with the register scan as the detector for the shape, not closed.
Any other engine writer setting a destructive status: enumerated in DESTRUCTIVE_WRITERS with wired:false and a stated reason, enforced by a scan so a new one cannot be missed by omission.
A raw Postgres connection, or a hand UPDATE atoms SET body = jsonb_set(...).
The factory's writers -- the two registers are not joined (leave_behind), and the factory's side is the enforceable cross-repo direction because hauska-engine is public and hauska-factory is private.
Deleting the declaration/guard/drift check, editing the declaration AND the pin's facts in one commit, or catching the guard's throw.
